candidate.answerReason: Integral interior angles occur exactly when n is a divisor of 360 with n≥3. There are 24 positive divisors of 360; removing 1 and 2 leaves 22.

methods.label: Count divisors using prime exponents
methods.explanation:
For an integer \(n\ge3\), the equal interior angles of a regular \(n\)-gon each measure
\[
\frac{180(n-2)}{n}=180-\frac{360}{n}
\]
degrees. This is an integer exactly when \(360/n\) is an integer, so we need to count the positive divisors of \(360\), excluding \(1\) and \(2\).

Factor
\[
360=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5.
\]
Every positive divisor has exactly one expression \(2^i3^j5^k\), where
\[
0\le i\le3,\qquad 0\le j\le2,\qquad 0\le k\le1.
\]
There are \(4\) choices for \(i\), \(3\) for \(j\), and \(2\) for \(k\), giving \(4\cdot3\cdot2=24\) divisors. Unique prime factorization ensures that all divisors occur and none is counted twice. Removing \(n=1\) and \(n=2\), which do not form polygons, leaves \(\boxed{22}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument combines the elementary polygon angle formula with prime factorization and independent exponent choices.

methods.label: List complementary factor pairs
methods.explanation:
The exterior angles of a regular \(n\)-gon are equal and sum to \(360^\circ\), so each is \(360/n\) degrees. An interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle add to \(180^\circ\). Thus the interior angles have integral degree measures exactly when \(360/n\) is an integer: \(n\) must divide \(360\), with \(n\ge3\).

We can count these divisors by pairing each divisor \(d\) with \(360/d\). Since
\[
18^2<360<19^2,
\]
every pair has exactly one member at most \(18\). Checking the integers from \(1\) through \(18\) gives all the pairs:
\[
\begin{gathered}
(1,360),\ (2,180),\ (3,120),\\
(4,90),\ (5,72),\ (6,60),\\
(8,45),\ (9,40),\ (10,36),\\
(12,30),\ (15,24),\ (18,20).
\end{gathered}
\]
There are \(12\) pairs, each containing two distinct divisors. Every divisor belongs to exactly one pair, so there are \(24\) divisors altogether. Excluding \(1\) and \(2\) leaves \(\boxed{22}\) possible side counts, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: This route uses exterior angles and an exhaustive factor-pair list, avoiding a divisor-count formula.

candidate.annotationRationale: The common target is identifying all admissible side counts as factors of 360. The interior-angle formula and prime-exponent divisor count belong to the first route; exterior-angle reasoning and factor-pair enumeration belong to the second. Prime factorization is therefore not imposed as a shared prerequisite.

review.mathematicalCheck: An interior angle is integral exactly when n divides 360, with n≥3. Prime-exponent choices give 24 divisors. Independently, the second method lists all 12 distinct factor pairs using 18²<360<19². Both counts exclude 1 and 2 to obtain 22.
review.levelCheck: Both methods use appropriate school geometry and elementary counting. Completeness and absence of duplicate counting are explained.
review.methodDistinctness: Prime-exponent counting and bounded factor-pair enumeration provide genuinely distinct, accessible counting methods.
